record.original_question: For homogeneous structures whose current big-Ramsey-degree proofs rely on forcing, can those arguments be replaced by proofs that are entirely combinatorial, including for k-clique-free homogeneous graphs with k >= 4 and other free-amalgamation classes where current methods do not yet provide such proofs?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.2. For results whose proofs use the method of forcing, find new proofs which are purely combinatorial.
This has been done for the triangle-free graph by Hubicka in [39], but new methods will be needed for k-clique-free homogeneous graphs for k >= 4 and other such FAP classes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A relational structure M is called homogeneous if every isomorphism between finite substructures of M extends to an automorphism of M. For a finite substructure A ⊆ M, the big Ramsey degree of A in M is the least integer T (if it exists) such that for every finite r ≥ 1 there is a coloring-bound T with the property that for every coloring c of the copies of A in M with r colors, there exists an isomorphic copy M' of M inside M on which the copies of A take at most T colors.

A class K of finite structures has the free amalgamation property if, whenever A, B₁, B₂ ∈ K with A embedded in B₁ and B₂, the free amalgam of B₁ and B₂ over A (gluing along A with no additional relations) again lies in K. The Fraïssé limit of such a class is a countable homogeneous structure whose age is K.

For each integer k ≥ 3, the Henson graph H_k is the Fraïssé limit of the class of finite K_k-free graphs (graphs containing no clique on k vertices). Existing proofs that the finite substructures of H_k (for k ≥ 4) and of various other Fraïssé limits of free-amalgamation classes have finite big Ramsey degrees use set-theoretic forcing as an essential ingredient.

Problem. For each k ≥ 4, find a proof, using only combinatorial methods (without invoking forcing), that every finite K_k-free graph has a finite big Ramsey degree in the Henson graph H_k. More generally, for Fraïssé limits of free-amalgamation classes whose finiteness of big Ramsey degrees is currently established only via forcing, produce purely combinatorial proofs of the same results.
artifact.category_tag: big Ramsey degrees of homogeneous structures
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Balko, Chodounský, Dobrinen, Hubička, Konečný, Vena, and Zucker has fully characterised big Ramsey degrees of Fraïssé limits of finitely constrained free-amalgamation classes in finite binary languages using combinatorial methods based on parameter spaces and the Carlson–Simpson theorem, rather than forcing. A 2025 preprint provides a self-contained combinatorial treatment for the universal homogeneous K₄-free graph, indicating the problem has been resolved combinatorially for Henson graphs and more general free-amalgamation classes.

status_evidence.title: Counting big Ramsey degrees of the homogeneous and universal K4-free graph
status_evidence.snippet: Big Ramsey degrees of Fraïssé limits of finitely constrained free amalgamation classes in finite binary languages have been recently fully characterised by Balko, Chodounský, Dobrinen, Hubička, Konečný, Vena, and Zucker.
status_evidence.claim: Combinatorial characterisation now covers K4-free homogeneous graph and free-amalgamation classes.

status_evidence.title: Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures: current trends and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work has relied on parameter spaces and the Carlson-Simpson theorem rather than on the Halpern-Läuchli theorem and the Milliken tree theorem.
status_evidence.claim: New combinatorial techniques replace forcing-based methods.
